title: Federal Register: Requirements for Additional Traceability Records for Certain Foods, final rule (FSMA section 204)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.
Review correction: distinguished historical economic analysis from separately sourced current timing.

publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government final rule with regulatory flexibility analysis
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency is also the party imposing or administering the requirement.
findings: FDA states: "Because some small firms may incur annualized costs that exceed 1 percent of their annual revenue, we find that the final rule will have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities."
The final rule exempts certain small producers (including small produce farms and shell egg producers) and certain small retail food establishments and restaurants.
FDA adopted a three-year compliance period for all covered entities.
FDA states that firms keeping paper records should be able to create the required sortable electronic spreadsheet from those records "under those limited circumstances".
limitations: Per-firm cost figures and the number of affected small firms were not extracted and are not recorded.
This source is the historical 2022 final rule, not current timing guidance. Later FDA timing is recorded separately in source-40ee46dd9d834b12.
Agency analysis; no independent measurement of actual burden.
